edits.issue: Recognition stated beyond fact_104: omits the condition that the marriage would also have been valid under Australian law.
edits.old: In most cases, yes: Australia generally recognises a marriage that was valid where it took place.
edits.new: In most cases, yes: Australia generally recognises a marriage that was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law.

edits.location: Step by step > Lodging your request in person, paragraph 3
edits.issue: 'Plan around two visits' is an unsupported inference. fact_02 and fact_10 say only that both lodge the request together in person; fact_11 gives an average of 4 to 6 months to the ceremony. Nothing sources two trips. Restate only the facts and send the couple to the Registro Civil or a notary.
edits.old: Living in Australia, plan this route around two visits: one to lodge the request together, and one for the wedding itself.
edits.new: Living in Australia, remember that you lodge the request together in person and the ceremony follows on average 4 to 6 months later, so ask the Registro Civil or a notary how this fits your travel.
